Life Esidimeni Part 3

By: Tarryn Crossman | Delivery

Proposal


Show:

Summary:
Focus on Patients, how they really died and the NGO's.


Further information:
Case studies
Norma - daughter relapsed in story 1. She has been returned to Siyabathanda. Norma will do spy cam to see what the conditions are now. Then Devi will approach Thembi for an interview: She has met me before, I spend the day with her under the guise of being a donor. I can maybe convince her to tell her side of the story, she was not paid by the GDOH for months.
Lucas - Died at Rebafenyi the NGO that Jack bloom sent me evidence on proving that the Police Major -general Sandra Malebe-Themba is the director and Tshwane ANC councillor is a board committee member. He died from 'falling' apparently, but was only found in the morning as no-one was on night duty.
Miriam's son Thabo - death report states "imbalanced electrolytes" which is dehydration and starvation
Nomvulo's Brother - is still at cullinan and will do spy cam footage. Getting thinner and thinner.
TBC: Patient died of Diabetes, as they were not given their medication
Precious Angel - another 2 patients
Bongani 28 still missing
Sophia - daughter Bertha committed suicide after being visited by officials from the GDOH and given medication instead of being institutionalised
Bophelong - I am looking for someone who may still be here. They say it is closed, but SADAG has reports that it is not.

We are still crawling through another list of like 30 patients from SADAG.

Specialists
Erik - Former head of Psychiatry at Life and he was against the move
Life - taking the patients back
Dr. Talatala - he can tell us from their history what care they should have been given. Bigger picture - mental health issues in SA and what needs to be done. This is a micrcosm for the state of mental health across the board
Bloom - I think we should interview him even if we don't use it, he has info and will share it better in a camera setup.
Premier of Gauteng - ? or someone about prosecution plans against specifically Precious Angel care and the Rebafenyi case. The fact that this must be costing more than being at life? We must work out the costs
Minister of Health was a crap interview human

Things to look into
estimated 3mill was authorised monthly for these patients, but the NGO's say they were never paid. Who was paid then? where did the money go?
It still does not make sense to me why the would take on the 100 mentally ill patients for 2700/month per patient. Maybe this needs to be investigated further
This NGO has been closed as of 31st Jan.

Press Release:


Mental Patient Death Toll Rises
South Africans were stunned when a health ombudsman report recently exposed that 94 psychiatric patients had died in the care of several under-equipped NGOs. That number has since skyrocketed to over 100 with the total death toll unclear as further deceased remain unidentified at mortuaries. What really went wrong? Two NGOs open up to Carte Blanche to reveal the shocking truth behind these tragic deaths and the neglect of South Africa’s forgotten state mental patients.


Script:


Timecode Description
00:00 Interview with Minister Aaron Motsoaledi Minister: Our primary existence is to preserve human life in this project it was the opposite.
00:10 Mariam : Thabo was my son, he had cerebral palsy. This wasn’t the time for Thabo to die, they caused his death by not taking care of him and not helping him when he needed it.
00:30 V/O with the statistics V/O: june 2015 the South African Society of Psychiatrist warns Gauteng health MEC multiple times about terminating the contract with Life Esidimeni.
00:40 Interview with Dr Talatala Talatala: Everyone who is in the mental health field is aware that there are no beds for ill patients. Remember we have not built any psychiatric facilities since 1994
00:53 V/O with Graph V/o: 21st of October 2015 and part of the deinstitutionalization program, MEC Mahlangu announces the termination of the contract with life Esidimeni.
01:02 V/O with Graph V/O: November 2015 to December 2015 various stake holder meet with the Department of health asking them to slow down the move
01:09 V/O with Graph V/O: 16th of March Gauteng Department of Heath announces the move of the first 54 adults life Esidimeni patients to a children facility called Takalani.
Again stake holders take the DoH to court they lose and the patients are moved. Later it would be revealed that 8 people died at Takalani.
01:30 Devi: SASOP, SADAG AND Section 27 these are the exact issues that they were trying to raise with the department
MEC: but I don’t know how you pre-empt issues and then worry…
Devi: because you can see it coming.
MEC: okay, unless they were fortellers
01:43 V/O with Graph V/O: from March to June 2016 over a thousand state psychiatric patients are moved to 27 NGO’s and three state Government Hospitals.
01:52 V/O with Graph V/O: 13th of september 2016 Gauteng health MEC Mahlangu announces in parliament that 36 patients have passed away since the move began.
02:00 MEC Mahlangu MEC: I continue to to say thawt we take full responsibility for that.
02:03 V/O with Graph V/O: 31st of January 2017 the MEC Qedeni Mahlangu resigns
02:10 V/O with Graph V/O: 1st of February 2017 the ombudsman report is released. And a total of 94 deaths are confirmed.
02:16 Professor Malegapuru Makgoba A total of 94 deaths and not 36 mentally ill patients have died during this process.
02:27 Devi V/O Devi: in his report the ombudsman states that only one of the 94 deaths he had calculated was as a direct results of a psychiatric disorder. This number has esculated to over a 100 who have died in these NGO’s since the move began.
02:44 Devi link Devi: when our investigations began, all the NGO we had contacted stated very clearly that they have been forbidden by the Department of health and Dr. Manamela specifically from speaking to the media. Finally two of the agreed to share their stories
03:01 Graph with V/O about the deaths that occurred in NGO’s Devi: the ombudsman reported that 80% of all 94 patients passed away in 5 NGO’s one of which was Siyabadinga where it was reported that 9 patients died. But to this day neither the ombudsman or anybody from the Gauteng Department of Health has been able to interview Dianne Noyile, the CEO of Siyabadinga.
03:23 Interview with Dianne Noyile CEO of Siyabadinga Devi: how did you feel when you read the ombudsman report?
Dianne: I felt that we were left out but there was report about us. But we were not asked anything so in my opinion that’s not fair because we took care of our patients, we love our patients we were at home with our patients
03:47 V/O: Siyabadinga was given a lease by the Cullinan care a Rehabilitation Centre to operate an NGO within the Government Institution. its purpose was to observe the patients from from CCRC who would loose bed due to an influx of Life Esidimeni patients but at last minute the GDoH begged her to take in 3 patients who had no where to go.
04:12 Dianne: they said you know what Dianne Life Esidimeni is watching us and this is the last day for us taking the patients if we don’t take them they are going to run straight to the media.
04:23 V/O: only after the patients arrived did Siyabadinga received their license from the Deputy Director health Hanna Jacobs
04:30 Dianne: she just came into the office and put it at the wall of the office. And this was noticed that this is not our license. Its not in our name and she answered calmly and said don’t worry we are going to fix it its just the DG and MEC can come on any time. So when they come they wont notice that its not in your name. the Lease agreement says we are given 4 wards and all of a sudden in June Henna jacobs and Dr Manamela came in and they said they are brinign another NGO which is Anchor. At this point in time we had 73 patients they literally moved the patients themselves to squash them in into the 2nd ward. So we had 73 patients in 2 wards, the patients were disorientated. The health care workers that day did not sleep at all.
Devi: what did it look like?
Dianne: a mess.
05:38 V/O: after writing to the MEC back in 2015, Dr. Talatala has closely followed the movement of the Life Esidimeni patients
05:46 Devi: Is it normal for psychiatric patients to live in a mixed ward Male and female?
Talatala: well that’s shocking, even in a boarding school you don’t mix them. some of them could be hyper sexual, they could be inappropriate towards the developed patients .
06:01 V/O: Shammah house was another NGO in Tshwane that was given 55 male and female from Life Esidimeni. They were licensed as an NPO to house homeless people and the poor but they were taking mental patients who were discharged from Weskoppies which they were not licensed to do. in 2015 Hanna Jacobs came to Shammah house to close down the facility.
06:25 Susan: Hanna came here to close down Shammah because we are not licensed they said are you prepared to take on people because we are closing down a Hospital and would you take some of these people so I said” well yes, I don’t want my place to be close”
Devi: so they were quit clear because it was either you take the patients or they close you down?
Susan: I belive so.
06:50 Talatala: we have heard those rumor that the NGO and some of the people who have never ran NGO they were actually forced to take patients
07:00 Susanne: well they came here and said this needs to be done. So we worked day and night to get the place ready
Niel: they had approved it before the patients because we said we are not taking patients in until the department has approved and for them the proof was when they issued the licences
Devi: so you complied with whatever they wanted?
Both: yes
Susanne: After everything was approved they start to complain about things. When they didn’t complain before they placed the people then everything must done now. This must be done and that when now. That when I told them in August please take your patients. I cant deal with this anymore and then the next day they came back and said they have no where to take these patients
07:54 Devi V/O V/O: in June 2016 Siyabadinga were also having serious issues with the Department of health
08: 00 Dianne: we did not have support from the Department. There were times where we didn’t have medication for about 2 weeks. I have sms’s that I sent to Dr. Manemela that we were struggling with medication. We were told that we must go to Refilwe Clinic and they said they were going to help us but when it was time for us to get the medication we were told that they don’t have the budget for us. I was going up and down to the regional pharmacy. Some eof the staff were going to the regional clinic,
Devi: so you had no medication? No psychiatric medication, no epileptic medication. there were 2 weeks when the patients didn’t get medication. I cannot imagine what it must have been like, psychiatric patients without their medication
Dianne: its scary
08:54 V/O: Dianne lost 4 patients during this time. She believes it was due to the lack of chronic medication for epilepsy and other conditions. This is all medication she shared with the Gauteng Department of Health.
09:04 V/O: on the 8th of July Siyabadinga was unexpectedly shut down.
09:09 Dianne: we were kicked out of the hospital
Devi: why?
Dianne: they said we were operating unlawful because we did not have a license. I think I was closed down because I was asking a lot of questions. I think the department of mental health are using it as an excuse but they know the truth.
09:28 V/O: according to the ombudsman report, the department knew that all 27 NGO’s weere operating without unlawful linceses as it was Dr. Manamela the Director of Mental Health who was the one issuing them asnd she was not authorised to do so.
09:43 Devi: after you were kicked out more patients died
Dianne: yes
Devi: Can you tell me about this?
Dianne: Im not really sure but the ones that I know of is Thabo.
09:56 Mariam: They phoned me on the 10th of August to tell me that he was sick. It was terrible. He couldn’t swallow. He was drinking water as if it was for the first time in his life. the next day I took him to Steve Biko and the doctor told me the chances he’d survive are very slim. The death report said Thabo had electrolyte imbalance and pneumonia.
10:29 V/O Devi link Devi: After losing 4 patients and operating on the same unlawful license, Shammah house is still opened. Currently they are housing 50 patients from Life Esidimeni. The latest death tool place here on the 12th of February 2017 his name was Michael
10:50 Devi Devi: Mosego house is a NGO situated in Krugersdorp it consists of 8 residential properties and is on of the NGO’s that the ombudsman recommended be closed immediately. Its estimated that 7 patients died here one of whom is Freddy Collets whose wife is still looking for answers.
11:08 Mari: The sister working there called me and said ‘Mari, Mari, if you want to see your man you better come’. She said ‘I beg you, don’t be long or you wont see your husband again’. She didn’t what they did to him. She wouldn’t give me details then we saw what he looked like. He looked bad, on his head he had an old scab you could see it was old they said that he fell, I don’t believe that. He had another one on his nose. On is ankles he had huge marks. Those werent shoe marks that caused those, I think they dragged him because he couldn’t walk anymore. It was a big shock for us because I caint believe they could do this to him in a month. Why didn’t they phone me at the beginning of the month and say come get your husband we don’t have food for him. Im telling you, he died of dehydration. His eyes just stared at you. His eyes didn’t move anymore, he was already half dead. All he could say was ‘Mari, kiss me’ that’s all he could say.
12:12 Devi: The national Minister of Health Aaron Motsoaledi explains what is next for the patients that are moved from Life Esidimeni almost a year ago
12:21 Devi interview with Aaron Devi: How many patients are still in these NGO’s?
Minister: there are about 700 and the work of relocating them will work some time next week.
Devi: where are they going to go to?
Minister: it seems they must go to any appropriate facility that has got the competence for professionalism and the skills, public and private. So Esidimeni itself is still an option. They said that it would tale about 8 weeks for them to reestablish then they said the first week meaning next week they will only accept 75
12:54 Devi: while the Gauteng Department of Health desperately tries to fix this mess theres so many family who are still trying to locate their loved one. There are bodies lying unidentified in mortuaries and hundred of patients are still in these NGO’s
13:10 Mari: Its been 7 months and I still don’t have any answers about why he died. For them its nothing, hes just a number. For us he wasn’t just a number
13:24 Mariam: when he was not blind he used to shed papers and roll it nicely neat and started playing with them and he used to do like this. I stopped working at 60 because I wanted to look after my son. That didn’t happen, he died two weeks before my retirement. Im trying to be strong

I think the department of mental health are using it as an excuse but they know the truth. 09:28 V/O: according to the ombudsman report, the department knew that all 27 NGO’s weere operating without unlawful linceses as it was Dr. Manamela the Director of Mental Health who was the one issuing them asnd she was not authorised to do so. 09:43 Devi: after you were kicked out more patients died Dianne: yes Devi: Can you tell me about this? Dianne: Im not really sure but the ones that I know of is Thabo. 09:56 Mariam: They phoned me on the 10th of August to tell me that he was sick. It was terrible. He couldn’t swallow. He was drinking water as if it was for the first time in his life. the next day I took him to Steve Biko and the doctor told me the chances he’d survive are very slim. The death report said Thabo had electrolyte imbalance and pneumonia. 10:29 V/O Devi link Devi: After losing 4 patients and operating on the same unlawful license, Shammah house is still opened. Currently they are housing 50 patients from Life Esidimeni. The latest death tool place here on the 12th of February 2017 his name was Michael 10:50 Devi Devi: Mosego house is a NGO situated in Krugersdorp it consists of 8 residential properties and is on of the NGO’s that the ombudsman recommended be closed immediately. Its estimated that 7 patients died here one of whom is Freddy Collets whose wife is still looking for answers. 11:08 Mari: The sister working there called me and said ‘Mari, Mari, if you want to see your man you better come’. She said ‘I beg you, don’t be long or you wont see your husband again’. She didn’t what they did to him. She wouldn’t give me details then we saw what he looked like. He looked bad, on his head he had an old scab you could see it was old they said that he fell, I don’t believe that. He had another one on his nose. On is ankles he had huge marks. Those werent shoe marks that caused those, I think they dragged him because he couldn’t walk anymore. It was a big shock for us because I caint believe they could do this to him in a month. Why didn’t they phone me at the beginning of the month and say come get your husband we don’t have food for him. Im telling you, he died of dehydration. His eyes just stared at you. His eyes didn’t move anymore, he was already half dead. All he could say was ‘Mari, kiss me’ that’s all he could say. 12:12 Devi: The national Minister of Health Aaron Motsoaledi explains what is next for the patients that are moved from Life Esidimeni almost a year ago 12:21 Devi interview with Aaron Devi: How many patients are still in these NGO’s? Minister: there are about 700 and the work of relocating them will work some time next week. Devi: where are they going to go to? Minister: it seems they must go to any appropriate facility that has got the competence for professionalism and the skills, public and private. So Esidimeni itself is still an option. They said that it would tale about 8 weeks for them to reestablish then they said the first week meaning next week they will only accept 75 12:54 Devi: while the Gauteng Department of Health desperately tries to fix this mess theres so many family who are still trying to locate their loved one. There are bodies lying unidentified in mortuaries and hundred of patients are still in these NGO’s 13:10 Mari: Its been 7 months and I still don’t have any answers about why he died. For them its nothing, hes just a number. For us he wasn’t just a number 13:24 Mariam: when he was not blind he used to shed papers and roll it nicely neat and started playing with them and he used to do like this. I stopped working at 60 because I wanted to look after my son. That didn’t happen, he died two weeks before my retirement. Im trying to be strong

Lucas - Died at Rebafenyi the NGO that Jack bloom sent me evidence on proving that the Police Major -general Sandra Malebe-Themba is the director and Tshwane ANC councillor is a board committee member. He died from 'falling' apparently, but was only found in the morning as no-one was on night duty. Miriam's son Thabo - death report states "imbalanced electrolytes" which is dehydration and starvation Nomvulo's Brother - is still at cullinan and will do spy cam footage. Getting thinner and thinner. Premier of Gauteng - ? or someone about prosecution plans against specifically Precious Angel care and the Rebafenyi case. The fact that this must be costing more than being at life? We must work out the costs Minister of Health was a crap interview human Things to look into estimated 3mill was authorised monthly for these patients, but the NGO's say they were never paid. Who was paid then? where did the money go? It still does not make sense to me why the would take on the 100 mentally ill patients for 2700/month per patient. Maybe this needs to be investigated further This NGO has been closed as of 31st Jan.
